Hi Markus,

Thanks for the pricing deck — two quick clarifying questions from procurement before we move to signatures:

1) How do you account for tokens when a single API call spans a long context (e.g., 12k prompt + streaming response)? Is that charged as a single session at the long-context rate or broken into atomicized billing units?

2) We heard about a "heartbeat offset" for lightly active sessions (prefix reuse + periodic keepalive). How does that interact with minimum-floor rounding? For example, if a conversation is active 10% of the time but has a kept-alive KV cache, are we billed for full context each hour or only microfloor units?

Procurement asks because we want to map line items to our internal chargeback model. We appreciate sample math if possible.

Attached is our preferred contract template and example invoice layout — procurement will want the invoice mapping to be clear.

Hi Jane — thanks, great questions. I pulled in Kim (sales) and Karthik (billing) for precise language. Below is a compact walkthrough plus two attached artifacts: "Billing-appendix-A.xlsx" with worked examples and "commit-layout.pdf" with invoice line mapping.

Short answers up front:
- Token accounting: charge is per-token (ingest + output) but we apply an atomicization step for very long single-context calls that exceed model slab thresholds. That means a 12k prompt is billed as a single request's tokens but normalized into our 16k slab for pricing if it crosses the slab boundary; we do not split a single logical call into multiple invoice lines unless the customer requests context slicing.
- Heartbeat offset: when a session maintains an active KV cache via heartbeats, we bill a microfloor per time window (configurable; default 1-hour window) plus an offset when prefix reuse is above the threshold. The offset reduces the effective billed context for repeated prefixes — effectively you pay the microfloor + incremental tokens for new content.

Example (see appendix sheet "Sample math - KV reuse"):
- Single long call: 12,000 tokens prompt + 3,200 tokens output = 15,200 tokens. For a model with a 16k slab, that rounds to 16,000 for slab pricing. You pay 16k token units at the model unit price.
- Heartbeat session: Conversation with 90% prefix reuse, kept alive for 24 hours, heartbeat every 30 minutes. Default microfloor is 1,000 tokens per hour. We bill 24 * 1,000 = 24,000 tokens for housekeeping floors; then incrementally bill only new tokens in generation calls. If KV reuse reduces repeated context by 70%, the effective incremental token charge is significantly lower.

Notes and options: we can offer an enterprise concession for pilot customers: a capped microfloor for the first 90 days (e.g., cap at 8,000 tokens/day) or allow an alternate billing mapping to "session-hours" for your internal chargeback reconciliation.

I'll summarize the sample invoice mapping across three SKU lines in the attached commit-layout.pdf. Kim — could you confirm the deal-level concession language that we can propose in the SOW? Karthik — please confirm the rounding rule language (round up to nearest slab/quantum) so we can include an explicit clause.

Thanks,
